summary: China's exports and car sales abroad boom while shoppers at home hold back before Double 11, AI chips sit in Hong Kong, and a Pakistani astronaut heads to Tiangong.
body: Two Chinas show up in this week's numbers. Abroad, business is booming: economists polled by Reuters expect October exports, due Tuesday, to be about a third higher than a year ago, and China's trade surplus this year is on track to pass $1 trillion, helped by the global AI building boom.[^1] Car exports jumped 68% to 932,000 in October, but car sales inside China fell 27%, the 12th monthly drop in a row, according to the China Passenger Car Association.[^2]

At home, people are cautious. Ahead of Double 11 (Nov 11), the biggest online shopping day, the South China Morning Post reports shoppers are tuning out: retail sales grew just 1.1% in the first three quarters.[^4] Second-hand home prices in 100 cities fell 6.7% from a year earlier, and families are rushing to pay off mortgages early; at three state banks in Shanghai, early repayments now top 2 billion yuan a month at each.[^4] My read: when home values fall, people save instead of spend, which is why China leans on exports.

In technology, about 600,000 Nvidia H200 AI chips are sitting in Hong Kong because Beijing has not approved large-scale imports, Reuters reports, as China pushes Alibaba, ByteDance, Tencent and DeepSeek to use Chinese-made chips.[^3] And in space, a Pakistani astronaut will fly to China's Tiangong space station on Shenzhou-24, the first foreign visitor to the station, AFP says; Pakistan's planning minister names Nov 25 as the date.[^5]

reads.summary: Young people buy outfits for under 50 yuan to wear once on a trip or for social media. A look at cheap fashion, skin worries and textile waste.
